claim: A bank of fog rolls in from one side, billowing across the surface in slow churning layers, with in-shader front-to-back depth.

q1_defects.answer: The round-2 blocker is FIXED. The hard vertical mid-quad seam — a near-black vertical canyon splitting the quad into a darker-left and brighter-right fog sheet — is GONE. idle.png and play-1/2/3.png all show one smooth continuous organic density field: soft cool-grey fog filling the quad evenly with billowing wisps, no vertical channel down the centre, no axis-aligned tile grid, no pasted-side-by-side edge. Nothing is cut off, misaligned, or low-contrast. bandingScore ~0.19 reflects organic fog detail, not a hard seam (judged by eye per caveat-a — no canyon/shelves visible). No console or network errors.
evidence: metrics: play-2 bandingScore=0.192 (organic, no hard seam by eye); consoleErrors=[] networkErrors=[]

q2_reads_as.answer: Yes — reads as a continuous rolling fog bank. effHue=220 effSat=0.08 is a soft cool desaturated grey, exactly fog/mist colour; the body is a churning continuous density field of soft-edged billowing wisps with no hard leading edge (a fairly even soft fill is acceptable for fog per the caveat). The headline round-2 failure (front edge reading as a dark canyon dividing two sheets) is resolved — the field is now seamless across the centre.
evidence: metrics: idle effHue=220 effSat=0.08 (neutral cool fog)

q3_discoverable.answer: Yes for the control a user would reach for. The labeled 'density' control sweeps obviously: low = nearly clear/dissipated (control-density-low.png near-black, meanLuma 7.6), mid = moderate fog (meanLuma 41), high = thick filled fog (meanLuma 55). Dragging 'density' gives immediate cause-and-effect. 'roll' and 'scale' show changed=false on the paused sweep (expected per caveat-b — roll is motion, scale is frequency; judged from play deltas, not paused stats) and do not mislead.

q4_responsive.answer: Responsive. Play frames differ — wisps drift and reform between play-1, play-2, play-3 (frameDeltaMag 1.23, 1.28, 3.37, all non-zero), the slow churning drift the claim describes. No identical/dead frames. Control apply latency ~573-612ms is acceptable.

q5_net.answer: PLEASED. A user would say: 'The fog looks soft and real and the weird dark seam down the middle is gone now — it's one smooth bank of grey fog that drifts and gets thicker or thinner when I drag the density slider.' The round-2 vertical-seam blocker is resolved and the organic body from round-1 is preserved.

flags.note: The fog fills the quad fairly evenly with no strong directional 'rolls in from one side' read — it looks more like ambient drifting fog than a bank entering from one edge. Acceptable for fog per the caveat, but a subtle directional gradient would match the claim's wording more literally. Subjective taste, not a blocker.
